small_guidance:
- The fused epilogue kernel is fine; ConvTranspose3d now dominates (fast_p≈0.47, runtime 21.8 ms vs 10.3 ms baseline). Tuning BLOCK_S/num_warps further on the GN kernel will not close the gap — the conv is the bottleneck.
- If you keep tuning the existing GN kernel, try BLOCK_S=S=padded next-pow2 of S (S=33*65*65=...) per group only when it fits; otherwise stick to BLOCK_S=2048 num_warps=8 num_stages=2 and ensure x is contiguous channels-first so loads coalesce along S.
- Add a `triton.Config({'BLOCK_S': 8192}, num_warps=16, num_stages=2)` candidate; output spatial volume is 32*64*64 = 131072 per group, so a wider block may reduce loop overhead.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.ConvTranspose3d` with a custom Triton kernel implemented as a scatter-add of the (input × kernel) outer product into the output grid, handling stride=2/padding=1/output_padding=0 in index math. This is where the headroom is.
- Fuse the bias add + Swish into the ConvTranspose3d kernel epilogue so the output written to global memory is already swish(conv_t(x)+b). Keep the GN+HardSwish as the second kernel (current one).
- Use channels-last 3D layout for both conv_t output and GN input so the C axis is contiguous; this lets GN's per-(N,G) reduction load CPG=4 channels in a single contiguous chunk and lets the conv-T scatter coalesce along OC.
